questions.q: Why do SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, and AVERAGEIFS exist alongside SUMIF, COUNTIF, and AVERAGEIF?
options: They handle multiple conditions evaluated together, which the single-condition -IF versions cannot do
They are simply faster versions of the same one-condition functions
They only work on Excel Tables, unlike the -IF versions
They replace VLOOKUP entirely
questions.explain: SUMIF/COUNTIF/AVERAGEIF handle exactly one condition. The -IFS versions extend the same idea to any number of conditions evaluated together, which is what most real analyst questions actually need.

questions.q: In `=SUMIFS(Sales[Amount], Sales[Region], "West", Sales[Year], 2024)`, what does the first argument represent?
options: The range that gets summed — it comes first in SUMIFS, unlike in SUMIF
The first condition to check
The criteria range for the region
The sheet name
questions.explain: SUMIFS puts the sum range first, then criteria-range/criteria pairs — the opposite argument order from SUMIF, which is a common source of mistakes when switching between the two.

questions.q: Why doesn't COUNTIFS need a 'range to aggregate' argument the way SUMIFS and AVERAGEIFS do?
options: Counting only needs to know which rows match the conditions — there's no value column being summed or averaged
COUNTIFS actually does require one, it's just optional
COUNTIFS can only count text values, not numbers
COUNTIFS ignores all criteria after the first one
questions.explain: COUNTIFS is just a list of criteria-range/criteria pairs — it counts rows that satisfy every condition, with no separate column needed since it isn't aggregating a value.

questions.q: What is the main downside of using a helper column with a flag formula instead of SUMIFS?
options: It adds an extra column that must be maintained and re-copied down as rows are added, instead of one self-contained formula
Helper columns are always slower to calculate than SUMIFS
Helper columns can't use the AND function
There is no real downside — they're equivalent in every way
questions.explain: A helper-column approach works but adds ongoing maintenance overhead. SUMIFS does the same multi-condition aggregation in a single formula that recalculates automatically as the source Table grows.

questions.q: Why does building SUMIFS/COUNTIFS/AVERAGEIFS against a real Excel Table (from Lesson 3) matter?
options: The formulas keep working correctly as new rows are added, without manually extending a fixed range reference
SUMIFS only works when the source data is a Table, never on a plain range
Tables automatically remove the need for any criteria arguments
It has no practical effect — Tables and raw ranges behave identically here
questions.explain: A Table's structured references (like Sales[Amount]) automatically expand as rows are added, so the aggregation formulas keep including new data without being rewritten — a raw range reference would need to be manually extended.
